; Disable rendering and local control, then enter the bank8 scene initializer. The reviewed
; continuation runs the full sprite animation and local sound sequence. Safe return through its
; stack-page marker write depends on the explicit artificial SP=$F8 entry contract; natural
; ending completion is not established.
; Continue scene setup after the reviewed initializer, hide OAM, request sound $41 and run
; palette, character and segmented-object animation phases. The final loop waits through the
; fixed NMI service and ticks this bank's sound driver. Entry/return safety depends on the saved
; artificial SP=$F8 contract; this is not proof of normal ending completion.
; Wait for the fixed NMI service and update sound repeatedly after the scene sequence.
; Fifteen coordinate/configuration bytes followed by the first byte of the next routine. The
; active initializer copies sixteen bytes starting here; that final copied source byte remains
; Code. This source boundary does not imply a sixteen-byte Data record.
; Wait for NMI, upload sprite palette and DMA page $02, then hide the next OAM buffer and reset
; its cursor. Tick sound and advance the scene frame counter. The wait service deliberately
; returns through the NMI stack contract, not an ordinary interrupt return.
; Move the hero to target X=$F4, hide OAM and place an additional record at ($78,$80). Finish
; with the forward palette ramp; the scene meaning of this pose remains uncertain.
; Run the short pose sequence, a bounded rising effect, then two full frame-counter cycles of
; alternating hero records.
; Reset the frame counter and run two 256-tick cycles. Every 32 ticks choose one of two effect
; positions/records while drawing hero record $0B.
; Advance one frame and select the alternating auxiliary record from frame bit 5.
; Three parallel two-byte arrays: X positions, Y positions and sprite record selectors. Frame
; bit 5 chooses one cell from each array.
; Draw the hero and an auxiliary record for 79 frames. The auxiliary X advances with the local
; phase; Y is hero Y minus $17. This is a scene-specific placement effect.
; Advance the rising-effect phase and stop at $50.
; Choose eight consecutive poses from SceneIntroPoseSequence using frame divided by eight, then
; leave the hero in record $0B. The selector sequence is bounded separately from the following
; routine.
; Draw each table-selected pose for eight frame counts.
; Eight consecutive sprite selectors, one per eight-frame interval in the introductory pose
; sequence.
; Align and step hero X, move to $F4, wait 128 ticks, then move from X=$0C to $3C. The helper
; compares X to a target byte; its CMP carry deliberately controls the signed direction of ADC
; Tick the scene until frame bit 7 becomes set: 128 increments from zero.
; Keep the scene and sound running throughout the wait.
; Round hero X up to the next four-pixel boundary, alternate records 5 and 6 at eight-tick gates,
; and advance X by four between gates.
; Hold record 5 until the frame counter reaches a multiple of eight.
; Hold record 6 at the next eight-tick gate, then advance X again.
; Choose a 32-phase walk record from (frame>>3)&31, render, and move X until it equals the
; target. CMP carry makes ADC #1 add one below the target and two above it; from $F4 the
; wraparound path is intentional arithmetic, not a signed decrement.
; Return once hero X equals the requested target.
; Thirty-two walking sprite selectors indexed by (frame>>3)&31; values select records 7..9.
; For the current selector, load per-object configuration and initialize four vertical segment
; positions to $F0. Draw hero plus four parts; move the first part upward by two every fourth
; tick until below $8A. Then run a 32-step hold, a 32-step pose cycle, and a downward exit.
; Exact character identities are uncertain.
; Draw all parts each tick; update segment following and move the leading part every fourth
; tick.
; Draw the extra configured record, ramp the palette forward, and reset the phase for the
; 32-step hold.
; Keep the five visible parts updated; advance segment following once per four scene ticks, for
; 32 steps.
; After the reverse ramp, redraw the segment group with the alternate extra record and apply the
; forward ramp.
; Use selector*8 plus phase/4 to choose hero poses. Every six ticks advance the segment-follow
; phase; stop after 32 steps.
; Redraw the group and move the leading part down by two every fourth tick until it reaches $F0.
; The trailing parts follow through the same gap-limited helper.
; Leave the hero visible for a final half-cycle before returning.
; Continue scene updates during the final 128-tick wait.
; Eight rows of eight pose cells. The object selector chooses a row; the 32-step phase divided
; by four chooses a cell. Each cell is a local pose offset 0..4.
; Sixteen repeated 0/1/2-valued bytes between the bounded pose grid and selector arrays.
; Neighboring consumers and patterns were inspected; a further pose row or original source
; schema is unresolved.
; Two parallel arrays of eight scene record selectors, indexed by the segment-animation
; selector.
; Eight four-byte palette records. Each starts with a separator/padding byte followed by the
; three colors consumed for that segment selector. The palette consumer reads the last three
; cells.
; Run the segmented animation once for each selector 0..7.
; The complete per-selector animation returns before advancing the selector.
; Advance an eight-phase displacement lookup and add its first three bytes to the shared
; horizontal base. For each successive vertical part, leave gaps below twelve unchanged;
; otherwise move the follower two pixels toward its predecessor. The negative-distance test uses
; ones complement, so its magnitude is one less than absolute distance.
; Compare the first follower gap against twelve before choosing its movement direction.
; Apply the same twelve-unit spacing rule to the second follower.
; Apply the spacing rule to the third follower and return.
; Eight four-byte entries selected by (wave<<2)&31. The consumer reads signed coordinate/phase
; increments from the first three bytes; the fourth is zero backing. Values describe the scene
; wave mechanics; no original curve generator is asserted.
; Carry chooses one of two four-entry palette ramps. Over 32 scene ticks, DMA OAM, upload
; palettes, tick sound and select a palette byte every eight ticks. The fixed wait helper
; preserves banks 8/9 under the reviewed entry contract.
; Save offset zero or four from entry carry before clearing the frame counter.
; Each iteration updates display and sound, then derives the four-step ramp index from frame/8.
; Return after the fourth ramp interval.
; Two four-step ramps. Frame divided by eight selects a step below four, then a saved 0-or-4
; offset selects the ramp.
; One palette-valued byte between independently bounded ramp selectors and color records. Its
; original padding or record role is unresolved.
; Nine triples of palette colors on a four-byte stride. The final triple ends this 35-byte
; range; no unneeded fourth byte of the ninth record is included.
; Over 72 ticks, select nine four-byte records with frame/8 and copy the first three bytes into
; palette slots 1..3. The fourth record byte is not consumed here.
; Render hero record zero before changing the next palette triple.
; Return when all nine palette phases have elapsed.

; Copy the local palette seed backward through sixteen bytes.
; Y wraps once per 256-byte page; advance only source high and repeat for sixteen pages.
; Return when the next delta-Y byte is $FF.
; A selects one of the supported pointers in SceneSpritePointers. Consume
; (deltaY,tile,attributes,deltaX) tuples, accumulate coordinates modulo 256 and append OAM
; records. Stop on a tuple-boundary $FF or cursor overflow. The forty-nine-word prefix and
; target records are bounded independently; no full arbitrary-byte selector domain is asserted.
; At tuple boundaries $FF ends the record; all other leading bytes are added modulo 256 to Y.
; Return after the OAM cursor wraps; already emitted sprites remain in the buffer.

; consumer or fill purpose.
; Write marker $36 at RAM $0102, then tail-call the scene graphics initializer. With the
; reviewed entry SP=$F8 this does not overwrite live return slots. That concrete precondition
; does not establish safety for arbitrary stack positions or normal ending reachability.
; Twenty-four zero bytes after a tail jump and before the unresolved truncated byte at $8600.
; Boundaries and neighboring control flow support generic noncode; fill purpose remains unknown.
; Unknown: A lone $86 precedes the coherent $8601 wrapper. It may be the tail of a truncated
; instruction; this byte has no supported instruction boundary or Data role.
; The $8600 byte could instead be literal backing. The known $8601 wrapper does not
; establish its predecessor; no independent origin or boundary identifies this byte.
; Load follower-three coordinates into the drawing accumulator and append the selected scene
; record. This coherent wrapper starts after the unresolved truncated byte at $8600.
; Hide all 64 OAM slots by writing Y=$F4 at every fourth byte of page $02. The X wrap ends the
; loop.
; Transfer sixteen sprite-palette bytes from scene RAM to PPU $3F10, reset the address latch and
; scroll, and disable PPU control. Rendering must already be disabled or the caller must supply
; a safe PPU access interval.
; Sixteen palette bytes copied by the duplicate initializer at $865A. They match the active
; palette; adjacent code is excluded.
; Copy sixteen bytes of the code at $8018 into RAM $50..$5F, then install the local sixteen-byte
; palette. The seed source remains Code despite this read. Upload sixteen pages from $A000 into
; PPU $0000 under banks 8/9; finish with control and scroll zero. The inline palette at $864A
; separates these code bodies.
